title: Python coordinator RELEASE ignores DAOSequence
description: Dual-impl of project-LICHEN-worker6-m557. python/src/lichen/link/address_assignment.py ShortAddressCoordinator.process() uses _last_sequence_by_eui only on ALLOCATE. RELEASE deletes the live mapping with no RFC 6550 wrapping freshness check, so ALLOCATE seq=1, RELEASE seq=2, ALLOCATE seq=3, then retransmitted RELEASE seq=2 still drops the seq=3 assignment. Apply the same rule as rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs: same sequence = idempotent copy, newer = new request, older/incomparable = ignore before mutating. Keep last sequence after RELEASE so a later stale RELEASE cannot clobber a newer allocation. Tests should cover that scenario plus stale ALLOCATE not renewing a lease.
notes: Implemented Python RFC 6550 Section 7.2 DAOSequence freshness before allocation/release mutation. Same-sequence retries are idempotent only when operation matches current state; older/incomparable requests cannot release or renew. RELEASE retains/persists the last sequence using backward-compatible SAT3 state tombstones (SAT2/SAA1 remain readable), including release-on-unmapped updates, atomic save failure, restart, wrap/window and deterministic concurrency coverage. Rust state-machine freshness matches, but its SAT2 tombstone restart gap is already tracked by open project-LICHEN-worker6-emcr; no C/Zephyr short-address coordinator analogue was found (C lollipop helpers exist in RPL only). Gates: address-assignment 48 passed; full Python link 804 passed, 11 skipped; Ruff and mypy clean; git diff --check clean.
